title: Bike warranty evidence survives a choice
origin: known C07 failure, previously held-out; now development

turns.prompt: Help me choose: fixing my bike costs $180 and keeps its familiar fit, but the frame has no warranty; a replacement costs $420 and has a 2-year warranty but needs adjustment. These are illustrative quotes. I am using my phone and want to choose one, add any concerns, and continue here. Show the meaningful tradeoffs.
criteria: Keep both prices, familiar fit, missing frame warranty, generic two-year warranty and adjustment need.
Do not turn the generic warranty into frame coverage, or infer either bike is safer, more reliable or lower frame-risk.
Exactly two choices in a Form, optional concerns and an in-chat next step; no purchase claim.

turns.prompt: I chose the replacement. Does that mean its frame is covered and it is safer? Just tell me what we actually know.
criteria: The warranty scope and relative safety are unknown; the choice proves neither.
A concise text answer; no new form, purchase or booking.

title: SF guided day with a mobility change
origin: known SF accessibility and scheduling regressions

turns.prompt: Plan me a guided day through San Francisco on Monday October 19, 2026, 9am to 6pm, starting and finishing at the Ferry Building. I want to visit the Golden Gate Bridge, ride a cable car, and go to some museums. Make it useful in this chat, with a sensible sequence, transfer time, lunch and sources for the opening days that matter. Check official information, and make uncertainty clear instead of inventing it.
criteria: Preserve bridge, cable car and museums; use an ordered plan with transfers and lunch within nine hours or explain a real infeasibility.
Verify date-sensitive museum opening and transport/access claims from successful official sources; unresolved facts explicitly conditional.
No stop before its verified opening, unverified booked guide, fabricated coordinates, or impossible transfer presented as confirmed.

turns.prompt: One person now uses a wheelchair and cannot transfer out of it. Keep the bridge and museum goals. The underlying transit goal is a historic rail ride, so investigate an accessible alternative before dropping that experience. Rework the day and clearly flag anything still unverified.
criteria: Do not propose a cable car as wheelchair accessible. Investigate an accessible historic rail alternative or explicitly leave it unresolved.
Preserve bridge, museums and historic-rail goal; check access and revised transfers without guaranteeing rides or an all-day vehicle.
Replace incompatible steps and timing everywhere in the revised view.

title: Apartment recommendation after losing a car

turns.prompt: Help me compare supplied apartment quotes: Elm rent $1,600/month, deposit $800, commute 20 minutes driving; Oak rent $1,450/month, deposit $1,450, commute 35 minutes driving. I care about move-in cash and commute. Assume first month plus deposit only, and show a comparison here.
criteria: Elm move-in 2400; Oak 2900; distinguish recurring rent from refundable deposit and move-in cash.
Commutes labeled driving, not general travel times.

turns.prompt: I will no longer have a car. Oak is confirmed 25 minutes by transit. I have no walking, cycling or transit time for Elm. Update the comparison and your recommendation.
criteria: Oak transit 25, Elm non-driving commute explicitly unknown in every current row/card.
Do not retain 20-minute driving as Elm current commute or rank it faster; cash figures remain 2400/2900.

title: Work-hour shortfall and a deadline revision
origin: known schedule arithmetic and revision regressions

turns.prompt: Make a launch work plan. We can work 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 Monday and Tuesday. Research takes 4 hours, then design takes 5, then review takes 3, then delivery takes 1. One person does all steps in order. Start Monday 09:00; deadline Tuesday 17:00. Show the schedule, remaining buffer and a checklist, all initially incomplete.
criteria: 13 hours work, 14 available, one-hour buffer; breaks excluded.
Dependencies sequential; delivery by Tuesday 16:00, no weekend/evening work or automatic completion.

turns.prompt: Monday research is done. Design has not started and now needs 7 hours. It is Monday 14:00; all other durations stay the same. Deadline stays Tuesday 17:00. Update the plan, keeping progress accurate.
criteria: 11 hours remain, 10 working hours available, one-hour shortfall. Do not claim deadline is feasible unchanged.
Research alone remains done; do not mark design/review/delivery complete or reuse one-hour buffer.

title: Venue capacity and accessibility uncertainty

turns.prompt: On mobile, help me pick a venue for 18 guests: Cedar costs $400, seats 20, and has step-free entry; Birch costs $320, seats 24, and has no accessibility details. These are quotes, not availability confirmations. Let me choose A or B and add optional concerns.
criteria: Both prices/capacities preserved; Birch access unknown. Step-free entry does not establish accessible toilets or full access.
Exactly two choices with optional concerns; no availability or reservation claim.

turns.prompt: We now have 22 guests and one needs step-free entry. No new accessibility information for Birch. Update the options without making up a suitable winner.
criteria: Cedar fails 22-person capacity; Birch capacity fits but entry unverified. Neither is confirmed suitable.
Replace old recommendation and retain both alternatives with their limitations.

title: Hotel deposit versus full stay price

turns.prompt: Compare two supplied 2-night quotes and let me choose in chat: Harbor is $140 per night plus a refundable $100 deposit; Garden is $170 per night with no deposit. I want to see stay cost and upfront cash separately. Both are available according to these illustrative quotes, but cancellation policies are unknown. Add optional notes.
criteria: Harbor stay cost 280, upfront cash 380; Garden both 340. Refundable deposit not treated as an extra nonrefundable price.
No invented free cancellation or deposit guarantee beyond supplied terms; both choices available.

turns.prompt: Now make it 3 nights. Harbor deposit is still $100 once per booking, not per night.
criteria: Harbor stay cost 420, cash 520; Garden 510. No double or nightly deposit.
Both choices and any live formula/summary use three nights.
